scope: Corollary 3.5 (Determinants for abelian covers) of the manuscript “Abelian covers, Gale correspondences, and the Hodge conjecture for powers” (preprints/Abelian-covers-Gale-correspondences-and-the-Hodge-conjecture-for-powers-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 032 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3467c8077855a568), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let a finite abelian group P act faithfully on a smooth connected projective complex curve C, and put B = C/P. For every character χ : P → k×, the line D(H1(C, k)χ) is CM-supplied. This includes the zero character spaces. For the trivial character the line is generated by a rational algebraic cycle class. For χ ̸= 1, let rχ be the number of branch points of C/ ker χ → B. Then dimk H1 (C, k)χ = 2g(B) + rχ − 2. The number rχ counts precisely the original branch points whose inertia is not killed by χ. For a fixed P, the CM sources for all these lines can be taken to be powers of one fixed product of Fermat-curve Jacobians depending only on P, not on the complex structure of C.
